sisr-qubo-from-binary-mask: Section 4.1, p.3: Eq. 3 and 4 define the binary-mask formulation the paper uses; quotes carry it.
sisr-three-algorithms: Section 4.2, p.3: the paper states its three algorithms share one formulation and differ in the optimizer.
sisr-classical-annealing-solver: Section 4.2, pp.3-4: states the scikit-learn Lasso solver and the qubovert simulated annealing it used.
sisr-qa-subproblem-size-32: Section 4.2, p.4 and Fig. 2: tabu seed, 32 selected variables, 32-size subproblems on a 512 by 512 Q matrix, all stated as the paper's own design.
sisr-qa-read-weighting-entropy: Section 4.2, p.5: defines the weights p_ij and the patch entropy H_i; 'can be defined, providing a metric' is the paper's own definition.
sisr-dictionary-training-setup: Section 5.1, p.5: 128 atoms, 69-image dataset of Yang et al. and the reason are the paper's own training setup.
sisr-hyperparameters: Section 5.1, p.5: lambda, mu and Nreads values stated as the paper's own settings.
sisr-test-cases: Section 5.1, p.5: three test cases and the run-time basis stated as the paper's own evaluation scope.
sisr-hardware-and-metric: Section 5.1, p.5: CPU, D-Wave Advantage 6.1 with 5760 qubits, Y-channel PSNR and factor 3 stated as the paper's own setup.
sisr-different-hardware-limit: Section 5.1, p.5: the sentence states the evaluation setup (different hardware per algorithm). It is not worded as a limitation, so the basis is setup, not stated limit.
sisr-synthetic-setup: Section 5.2, p.6 and Fig. 3 caption: 756 by 100 Gaussian matrix, 36/720 split, 10-atom sparsity and 20 datasets stated as the paper's own numerical setup.
sisr-robust-prediction-insufficient-evid: Section 5.4, p.8: the authors state evidence for robust prediction is insufficient because QPU access was limited. Type should be 'measured' (a limit on their own results).
sisr-limited-qpu-access: Footnote 1, p.1: the authors state limited QPU access makes it difficult to demonstrate the true potential on time and accuracy.
choy-maxcut-ising-mapping: Section II, p.2: defines Max-Cut on a weighted graph and states the Ising-type Hamiltonian H_C (Eq. 1) it uses.
choy-qaoa-ansatz-definition: Section II, p.2, Eq. 4: defines the Trotterised ansatz up to depth L from the equal superposition state.
choy-classical-simulation-scope: Section II, p.2: states it simulates the measurement classically and minimises the expectation of H_C (Eq. 2 and 3).
choy-lad-lmin-definitions: Section II, p.2: defines L_ad and L_min and states L_ad >= L_min.
choy-search-method: Section II, pp.2-3: basin-hopping with GMIN, parameter-shift gradients, discrete path sampling, disconnectivity graphs, all stated as the paper's own method.
choy-basin-hopping-parameters: Appendix A, p.10: convergence criterion, temperature, move size and saving threshold stated as its own settings.
choy-regular-graphs-setup: Section III.B, p.5: states it analysed all connected 3-regular unweighted graphs with 6 and 8 vertices, L = 1 to 4.
choy-expectation-threshold-definition: Section III.B, pp.6-7: defines the thresholds via convex hull intercepts at p_op = 0.5 and d1, d2.
choy-g2-g5-setup: Section III.C, pp.7-8 and Fig. 8: x = 0,3,4,5 give G2 to G5; G5 has the other correct solution and G4 has both. The G3 solution |abab> follows from the text ('both sets of graphs have |s> = |abab>').
choy-future-work-qml: Section IV, p.9: states the plan to extend to QML algorithms such as VQCs. A statement of intent, as scope.
choy-setup: Appendix A, p.10: 10,000 basin-hopping steps per run for K3-K8, 6a-8e and G2-G5 with GMIN, as stored.
qtg-aam-qaoa-construction: Abstract p.1 and Section IV-A: AAM-QAOA is the paper's own construction from the QTG and Grover-mixer QAOA.
qtg-knapsack-definition: Section III-A, p.2, Eq. 1: defines the 0-1 knapsack problem and its ILP.
qtg-lazy-and-very-greedy-definitions: Section III-A, p.2: describes LG and VG. The superset property follows at once from the stated rules (VG only differs by skipping and continuing).
qtg-qaoa-general-design-definition: Section III-C, p.3, Eq. 3 to 5: defines the QAOA state with 2q parameters and the diagonal objective Hamiltonian.
qtg-grover-mixer-definition: Section III-E, p.5, Eq. 17 to 19: defines the Grover mixer and GM-QAOA.
qtg-modified-qtg-for-mixer: Section IV-A, p.5: states the dropped profit register, classical average profit, zero-initialised capacity register and the changed control condition c-tilde <= c - w_m.
qtg-parameter-optimization-setup: Section IV-B, pp.5-6: grid-search initialisation after van Dam et al., NLopt constrained Powell and layer-wise initialisation for higher q, stated as its own procedure.
qtg-objective-by-sampling-feasibility-te: Section IV-B, p.6: states the sampled objective estimate and the classical feasibility test (infeasible gets zero).
qtg-simulation-technique-scope: Section IV-C, p.6: states which simulator is used for each method and the restriction to the feasible subspace.
qtg-mixer-criteria-iff: Section V-A, pp.6-7: derived in the text (Eq. 24 to 27) for each criterion, both directions ('Conversely...'), with the criteria stated. Not labelled a theorem, but the proof is in the paper.
qtg-projector-feasible-iff: Section V-A, p.7, Eq. 25 and 26: derived in the text for arbitrary psi in the feasible subspace; the condition is exact (the sum must vanish for all psi).
qtg-convergence-limited-practical-implic: Section V-B, p.9: the authors state the convergence result is purely theoretical and has very little implication at finite depth. Type should be 'theoretical'.
qtg-metric-and-reference-solver: Section V-B, pp.7-8: defines the global approximation ratio against the COMBO optimum and states no randomization in the subroutines.
cimini22-model-free-protocol: Abstract p.1: states its own method (NN trained on experimental data for the Bayesian update, RL for feedbacks).
cimini22-smc-no-resampling: Extension to adaptive regime, pp.3-4: QInfer SMC with fixed particles, resampling removed, distributions shifted by the control phases (Eq. 6).
cimini22-single-phase-setup: Single phase estimation section, p.4: r = 10, N_phi = 100, 100 phase values, 30 repetitions, SNL as the bound, stated as its own test.
cimini22-multiparameter-grid-setup: Extension to real scenarios, p.6: N_phi = 20, 20 cubed triplets, r = 1000, training on experimental data for 10 outputs.
cimini22-two-photon-ten-outputs: Extension to real scenarios, pp.5-6: d = 10 outputs (4 plus 6), unambiguous range of pi, training over 2 pi. These are the paper's own device and design statements.
cimini22-protocol-run-offline: Extension to real scenarios p.6 and RL section p.7: the protocol and the RL training are run offline on a measured grid.
cimini22-rl-cem-and-reward: RL-based design heuristics, p.7, Eq. 8: cross entropy method and the reward from [49], stated as its own choice.
cimini22-rl-network-and-training-setting: Methods p.11 and Supplementary Note 2 p.14: layer sizes, activations, observation vector, sigma = 0.5, 10% elite. The episode count prints as '104'; main text p.7 (rendered) shows 10 to the fourth, so the value's reading is right.
cimini22-nn-architecture-training: Methods pp.10-11: 5-layer keras network with three 64-node hidden layers, 256 batches, 60 epochs, cross-entropy, ADAM.
cimini22-benchmark-setup: Experimental results, p.7 (rendered): benchmark on a simulated ideal 4-arm interferometer, 10 to the fourth episodes, same particle count (10^3) as the NN approach.
cimini22-random-feedback-saturation-foot: Note [60], p.12: the authors state random feedbacks saturate here only through implicit knowledge of the true parameters. A caveat on their own result. Type should be 'measured'.
cimini22-device-description: Materials and Methods, p.10: 3.6 cm 4-arm interferometer, femtosecond laser writing, 785 nm, 12 shifters (3 phases, 3 feedbacks).
cimini-setup: The narrowed value is right: Conclusions pp.9-10 state the sensor and that the experiment trains on experimental data; Experimental results p.8 says the benchmark simulations train the NN on simulated data from the ideal likelihood.
cimini23-cost-function-trace-inverse-fim: Results, p.2: states its cost function (trace of the inverse FIM), direct FIM evaluation from data and use of the parameter-shift rules.
cimini23-nelder-mead-choice: Results, pp.2-4: states it used Nelder-Mead to cut experimental points and tested COBYLA. The value reports the authors' own description of the algorithm, which is accurate.
cimini23-nelder-mead-restarts: Supplementary Note 2, p.11: random tetrahedron simplex and 3 repetitions, taking the lowest cost, stated as its own procedure.
cimini23-optimization-not-always-global-: Supplementary Note 3, p.12: the authors state that repeated optimisation does not always reach the global minimum. Type should be 'measured'.
cimini23-photon-source-and-device: Methods, p.8: SPDC type I source at 808 nm, 3.6 cm chip with eight thermal shifters, 2.5 dB losses, 4 fiber beam splitters and 8 detectors.
cimini-experiment-scope: The widened value is right: Experimental results p.4 gives M = 50 and 30 repetitions; the Fig. 4 caption p.6 gives the 10 two-photon configurations and 6 single-photon triplets.
cimini-method-setup: Abstract, p.1: states its own hybrid feedback loop, parameter-shift reconstruction of the FIM and the derivative-free optimizer, as stored.

theory_low.choy-complete-graph-solution-count: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section III.A p.3 says 'it follows' with no derivation. The even-N formula is also garbled in the text layer (square lost).
theory_low.qtg-convergence-conclusion: Section V-A, p.7: the conclusion rests on [14, Theorem 12], which the paper cites and does not state or prove. The paper only checks the criteria. Proved elsewhere.
theory_low.aam-qaoa-converges-high-depth: The narrowed value is right by Section V-A and V-B. The convergence rests on [14, Theorem 12], cited and not proved here, so it is not a proved result.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.cimini22-qcrb-value: Materials and Methods, p.10: the bound 2.5/N is stated as computed from the QFI matrix, but the paper shows no derivation and gives no matrix. A stated computed value, not a proved result, and not a limit of the paper.
theory_low.cimini23-two-photon-four-term-rule: Gradient section, p.3: 'we thus prove' is a check of the spectrum against the four-term rule of cited work (Eq. 9, reference in Methods and SI). The rule is not proved here.
